title: Exception Chaining and Causes
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of exception chaining and causes and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—preserving the original cause—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study exception chaining and causes with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you report and recover from expected failures while ensuring resources are released. In this lesson, focus on preserving the original cause and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Exceptions describe abnormal or rejected operations. Catch an exception only when you can recover or add useful context, preserve causes, and prefer try-with-resources for closeable resources. Apply that reasoning specifically to preserving the original cause and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect preserving the original cause with wrapping exceptions at abstraction boundaries before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.

common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
